newsitem.title: CHINA: HK's Hang Seng extends gains, tops 16,000.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng extends gains, tops 16,000.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index extended its gains on Wednesday morning, cresting 16,000 points for the first time ever on a positive outlook for the property market, brokers said.
The index then headed higher, topping 16,011 points for a gain of 239 points, or 1.52 percent.
The property sector led the market, advancing 2.89 percent.

"The market is up for two reasons," said James Robertson, vice president at Salomon Brothers. "First, the HKMA (Hong Kong Monetary Authority) seems loathe to commit themselves to restrictive practices."
On Monday, Hong Kong's de facto central bank said it was not necessary to require banks to tighten their mortgage lending.
"Second, valuations don't look too tight," said Robertson, adding the market continued to track the U.S. bond market.
The 30-year U.S. Treasury rallied to close Tuesday trading at 103-8/32 to yield 6.38 percent. -- Kathleen Kearney (852) 2843 6933
